posts.author: Kabir_B
posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — For me, one thing I really enjoy is just observing things around me. Sometimes what you see in your daily life can be a pretty good research tool, especially for consumer-facing businesses. Of course, you have to filter out the noise and not take one observation as a conclusion. The most annoying part for me is probably figuring out which information actually matters and which is just noise. There is so much data and commentary available that sometimes filtering it is harder than finding it.

posts.author: DishantSR
posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — My workflow is fairly boring, but it cut my tab count a lot. I start with 10 years of financials and the peer table on Screener, and judge ROCE against the company’s own history and its 3–4 closest peers rather than as an absolute number. 18% is strong for a capital-heavy business but fairly ordinary for an asset-light one. posts.text: What's the most annoying part of researching an Indian stock? — I research Indian stocks regularly, and my process is held together by tabs and spreadsheets.
